text: . Benchmark domestic equity indices slumped over 1.6 percent today. The Sensex tanked 1, 248 points to close at 73, 581 while the Nifty plunged 384 points to settle at 23,063.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index shed 2.3 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index lost over 1.5%.This morning, Markets opened with a gap-down as spike in bond yields, elevated crude oil prices and a sell-off in banking and insurance stocks weighed on the indices. The Sensex and Nifty remained under pressure throughout the session, with sell-off intensifying during the second half of the trade.In the Sensex pack, 29 out of 30 companies logged losses with NTPC remaining unchanged. Among the top under performers, Bajaj Finance lost 5.5%, Axis Bank declined 4.7 per cent and Bajaj Finserv fell 4.1 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top losers, Mid-Small Private Banks declined 2.8 per cent, Housing Finance lost 2.6 per cent and Financial Services shed more than 2.3 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,884 companies declined, 1,473 advanced and 216 remained unchanged.

. The Bangladesh Government is committed to ensuring a safe, peaceful and festive environment for the celebration of Durga Puja 2026 across the country, Religious Affairs Minister Mohammad Shamim Kaiser has said.The Minister made the remarks at an inter-ministerial preparatory meeting to review arrangements for Durga Puja 2026 yesterday. Security has also been stepped up across the country to ensure that the upcoming Durga Puja is celebrated in a peaceful, festive and secure atmosphere.The State Minister said the government is committed to ensuring the safe and festive celebration of Durga Puja, described as the main religious festival of the country’s Hindu community. He directed relevant authorities to ensure the smooth distribution of grants from the Puja Welfare Trust to puja committees across the country.He also stressed enhanced vigilance by local administrations and law enforcement agencies in view of the increase in the number of puja mandaps. The State Minister called for maintaining social and religious harmony and urged people to respect traditional practices, including maintaining silence during the Azan and prayers.He directed intelligence and law enforcement agencies to take immediate legal action against those spreading rumours through old or edited content on social media and called for impartial investigations into any untoward incidents. Representatives of various ministries, security agencies and Hindu, Buddhist and Christian organisations attended the meeting.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended on a positive note today. The Sensex rose 315 points to close at 73,896. The Nifty gained 77 points to settle at 23,141. The broader market at the National Stock Exchangedisplayed mixedtrend. The Midcap 100 index dropped over 0.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index rose more than 0.1 per cent.In the forex market, the rupee appreciated by 14 paise to trade at 95 rupees and 82 paise against the US dollar.In the global crude oil market, Brent Crude was trading one per cent down at 105 US dollars and five cents per barrel, while WTI Crude was trading 1.7 per cent lower at 92 US dollars and 99 cents per barrel in intra-day trade.At the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the October contract was trading 0.7 per cent up at 1,51,709 rupees per 10 grams, and Silver for the December contract was trading 1.3 per cent higher at 2,36,574 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.For more updates about the market activities, tune in to Akashvani’s bilingual programme ‘Market Mantra’ at 6:30 PM this evening.

. National Investigation Agency NIA today arrested four individuals in connection with their relation with terrorist organisation Jama’at Mujahideen Bangladesh (JMB). The agency today conducted raids in many places in West Bengal, including Purba Bardhaman, South 24 Parganas and South Dinajpur districts. NIA arrested Piar Mohammad Sheikh an imam from Purba Bardhaman, Jumman Sheikh a tailor, Sahrul Purkayet an app bike driver and Abdul Rafique from South 24 South Parganas district.The investigation agency is searching for any link to the terrorist organisation JMB and Ansarullla Bangla Team. This raids have been conducted after some persons were arrested in Assam early this year. NIA today searched at Mundehar village of Banshihari of South Dinajpur district for Mujibar Rahman who is absconding.

. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has highlighted India’s ability to attract foreign capital with its broader manufacturing and overall reforms. Addressing the 13th PAFI annual forum in New Delhi, Mr Nageswaran emphasized that the most important thing for the industry is global competitiveness. He added that the global environment in which investment decisions are made has now shifted, making it important to assess India’s foreign direct investment performance in that context.Mr Nageswaran also pointed to investor protection, tax-policy certainty and consistency, and availability of skilled talent and logistics as other factors that can influence investment decisions. He noted that changing global interest-rate environments could also have a significant bearing on the cost of capital and cross-border investment flows.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have offloaded Indian equities worth 17,131 crore rupees in September so far. According to the latest depository data, out of the total net outflows, 25,682 crore rupees were withdrawn through sales on stock exchanges, as geopolitical uncertainty, elevated US bond yields, and crude oil prices weighed on investors’ risk appetite. However, the trend of FPI investment through the primary market has continued this month, with FPIs infusing 8,551 crore rupees in the primary market in September so far.Meanwhile, Foreign investors also extended their selling to the debt market during the period under review. In September so far, outflows from the debt securities through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) stood at 7,385 crore rupees. FPIs have withdrawn 3,021 crore rupees through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR) and 1,889 crore rupees through the General Limit route.

. The Consulate General of India in Dubai has organised a series of tree plantation drives at universities across Dubai as part of the ongoing Seva Pakhwada.Consul General of India in Dubai, Dr. E. Vishnu Vardhan Reddy, participated in plantation drives at Dubai campuses of various universities including BITS Pilani, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Amity University and University of Dubai. Consuls and other officials of the Consulate also participated in the drives, engaging with students, faculty and institutional partners to promote environmental awareness and action.The tree plantation initiatives reflect the spirit of Seva Bhav and a shared commitment to environmental sustainability, nurturing greener communities and contributing towards a sustainable future and the vision of Viksit Bharat.The Indian Consulate in Dubai has organised a series of programmes as part of Seva Pakhwada, to promote the spirit of service, community participation and national commitment.

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr L Murugan has called upon young creators to harness artificial intelligence as a tool for innovation and empowerment. Addressing the YouTube Impact Summit 2026 in New Delhi yesterday, the Minister highlighted the growing role of India’s digital and creative economy in driving economic growth, employment and global cultural outreach. He emphasised that technology changes rapidly, but constitutional values must endure.Dr Murugan highlighted the relevance of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity in India’s digital transformation. The Minister noted that content produced in India receives over 15 per cent of its watch time from audiences outside India, while more than 18 thousand Indian YouTube channels have crossed one million subscribers. Dr L Murugan also highlighted initiatives including WAVES, IICT, Create in India Challenges, Gems of India, WAVES Bazaar, MyWAVES and Creator’s Corner to strengthen pathways for identifying, developing and connecting creative talent with markets.<

Several Kashmiri political leaders, international human rights defenders, journalists, civil society representatives and activists today strongly condemned Pakistan over escalating human rights abuses in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) during an international conference held at the Geneva Press Club. The conference was organised by United Kashmir People’s National Party (UKPNP) on the sidelines of the ongoing 63rd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC) in Geneva.According to the UKPNP, the participants sharply criticised reported extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, communications blackouts and allegations of excessive use of force by Pakistani security forces in PoK.During the meeting, the UKPNP called for independent international investigations, accountability for those responsible for unlawful killings, justice for victims’ families, the release of arbitrary detainees and the restoration of fundamental freedoms in PoK.The conference also highlighted the demands for democratic self-rule, ownership of natural resources, freedom of movement, freedom of expression, stability and the rule of law in the occupied territory.The UKPNP reiterated its opposition to terrorism, extremism, political violence and the use of PoK as a weapon for geopolitical interests.

. India’s industrial output, as measured by the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), grew by 8% year-on-year in August this year. The latest data indicate that industrial activity continued to expand at a healthy pace, with the upward revision in July’s IIP growth to 7.4% from the earlier estimate of 6.7%.According to government data released today, electricity and gas supply recorded strong growth of 12.3% in August, while manufacturing, which carries the heaviest weight in the index, expanded by 9%. Water supply, sewerage and waste management also registered healthy growth of 6.3%. However, the mining sector remained a laggard, contracting by 5.6% during the period under review.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe and Tamil Nadu and some parts of North-Eastern states today.IMD has also forecast thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Puducherry, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura today.For Delhi, the weather department predicted a clear-sky day today with a maximum temperature of around 32 to 34 degrees Celsius and a minimum temperature to remain around 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

The traditional musical instrument Mandar, deeply rooted in the folk culture and tribal life of Jharkhand, has received official recognition with a Geographical Indication tag.The traditional folk instrument Mandar of Jharkhand has been accorded a GI tag, giving legal recognition to its distinctive geographical and cultural identity. The Geographical Indications Registry of the Government of India, based in Chennai, has granted the GI tag to ‘Mandar of Jharkhand’.The application for the GI tag was filed on 24th September 2021. Its traditional craftsmanship, use of locally sourced red clay, indigenous manufacturing techniques and distinctive sound were cited as key features supporting the application.The GI recognition is expected to give the products made by traditional Mandar artisans a distinct identity linked to Jharkhand and provide a stronger foundation for expanding their reach in domestic and international markets under an officially recognised GI status. ‘Mandar Samrat’ Manpuran Nayak described Mandar as an integral part of Jharkhand’s cultural heritage. He said that the GI recognition is a tribute to the ancestors and the soil of Jharkhand.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar said that India’s relationship with China is better today than it was last year. Speaking at an event organised by Asia Society in New York, Dr Jaishankar said the relationship started improving once the border standoff was resolved. He said that India has long been telling China that a dip in bilateral relationship does not help either country and a long standoff does not serve the interests of any nation.Speaking about the India-US relationship, and the trade deal negotiations, the External Affairs Minister said both nations have reached a situation where there is an understanding on the trade agreement. He pointed out that India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, and small factories. He added that apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production and the nature of society are very different. He said a trade negotiation required a certain amount of patience and detailing to see it through. He admitted that tariffs did create a bump for the relationship last year.Dr Jaishankar also highlighted the issue of terrorism, saying it is a particularly important issue for India. He remarked that there is not enough understanding or empathy from the US side regarding that. The External Affairs Minister stated that the Russia-Ukraine and the Iran-Gulf conflicts had a devastating impact on Global South economies. He expressed concern about the energy situation, saying the market is very tight. He further stated that if people play politics with it, it adds to the market complications and drives up prices at a time when people should be stabilising prices. He also cautioned that there is likelihood of a major food crisis, and significant fertiliser shortages, in the coming months.

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has signed a 50-million-dollar loan agreement with Modern Syntex Limited (MSL) to expand energy-efficient polyester chips production in Bangladesh.Under the Modern Energy-Efficient Polyester Chips Manufacturing Project, MSL will increase its polyester chips production capacity from 107 tonnes to 407 tonnes per day. The project will also refinance short-term local working capital loans.The expanded facility in the Mirsarai Economic Zone in Chattogram will produce high intrinsic viscosity polyester chips used in higher-value textile and apparel products.ADB said the project will help strengthen Bangladesh’s textile value chain by increasing domestic production of polyester chips and reducing dependence on imported synthetic inputs. It is also expected to shorten supply-chain lead times and improve efficiency for textile manufacturers.The project will introduce energy-efficient machinery, saving an estimated 4,840 megawatt-hours of electricity and reducing around 2,222 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions annually.The project is expected to create new jobs, with measures to promote greater participation of women through inclusive recruitment practices.

India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. India and Saudi Arabia reviewed cooperation in defence, security, trade, investment, energy, technology, healthcare and education. During a meeting with Saudi Finance Minister Mohammed Aljadaan on the sidelines of the AIIB Annual Meeting in Doha, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman described Saudi Arabia as a trusted and valued strategic partner of India. They welcomed the successful conclusion of negotiations on the India-Saudi Arabia Bilateral Investment Treaty, aimed at providing a stronger and more predictable framework for investments.Ms. Sitharaman also met Switzerland’s AIIB Governor, Ambassador Pietro Lazzeri, and discussed investment opportunities in India, including through NIIF and GIFT IFSC. She held talks with Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle on flood recovery and bilateral projects. They also discussed the early operationalisation of the UPI-NPI digital payment linkage.

In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index tumbled 1.6%, while the Smallcap 100 index tanked 1.8%.In the Sensex pack, 29 of the 30 constituent companies logged losses, with Infosys emerging as the lone gainer, rising 0.2%. Among the top underperformers, Larsen and Toubro slumped 2.8%, PowerGrid declined 2.6%, and Adani Ports fell 2.4%.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, all 28 sectors edged lower. . Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat felicitated 20 Award-Winning Artists at the 65th National Exhibition of Art in New Delhi yesterday. The Lalit Kala Akademi organised the exhibition. Addressing the gathering, Mr Shekhawat highlighted the significance of bringing together creativity and sustainability.He said the Seva Hi Sanskriti initiative, organised on the occasion of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday, demonstrates how creativity and the spirit of service can come together meaningfully. He appreciated the Lalit Kala Akademi’s efforts across its various verticals, including the Waste to Wonder initiative, which gives discarded materials a new artistic expression and highlights the role of art in promoting sustainability.

National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) Managing Director and CEO Dilip Asbe today said around 75 per cent of transaction volumes would fall outside the scope of the new merchant discount rate (MDR) regime, as 96 per cent of transactions are below 2,000 rupees.Addressing the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave in Mumbai, Asbe said there is “huge miscommunication and misinformation” surrounding the MDR regime and that NPCI and the government is trying to provide clear information.Mr Asbe clarified that the new regime will not hurt UPI volumes because most of the MDR will come from merchants who already accept credit cards and therefore, already pay MDR.

. The government has notified the new Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) norms for passenger vehicles. They will replace the existing CAFE norms with effect from 1st April 2027 and remain applicable up to 31st March 2032.It will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. The new framework provides greater regulatory clarity and a stable policy framework for the automobile industry. It also facilitates technological innovation and support the continued evolution of India’s passenger vehicle sector towards greater energy efficiency and lower fuel consumption.According to Ministry of Power, the new CAFE framework will drive progressive improvements in fuel economy through year-on-year tightening of targets across all five years. The fuel-consumption benchmark is tightened from 3.9 litres per 100 km in 2027-28 to 3.32 litres per 100 km in 2031-32, representing an improvement of around over 16 percent over the period.The revised target line has also been flattened to provide a more balanced, weight sensitive approach, with relatively softer targets for lighter vehicles and greater fuel efficiency requirements for heavier vehicles. Power Ministry stated that the new norms provide flexibility to manufacturers to adopt cleaner technologies, alternative fuels and other innovative solutions. The new CAFE framework promotes technological innovation in new technologies such as Solar reflective paints, advance glazing, high efficiency air-conditioning for improved fuel efficiency and India’s energy security and sustainability objectives.

In the Asian Games 2026, Neeru Dhanda has made history by becoming the first Indian shooter to win a gold medal in the women’s trap individual event.This came after she carried India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event with Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer. The Indian trio finished with a combined score of 328 points to secure the silver, finishing three points ahead of Kuwait, who took bronze with 325. China won the gold medal with a score of 346.In Boxing, Parveen Hooda and Ankush Panghal have stormed into the gold medal bouts of their respective weight categories with semifinal wins at Nishio today. Parveen defeated China’s Li Shu 5-0 in the 65kg semifinal, before Ankush came from behind to out-punch reigning 75kg world champion Uzbekistan’s Fazliddin Erkinboev 4-1 to book his place in the 80kg summit clash.In athletics, India secured a double podium finish in the men’s javelin throw. Yashvir Singh won the silver medal with a personal-best effort of 85.72 metres, while Rohit Yadav claimed bronze with a throw of 84.35 metres.In the men’s long jump, Sreeshankar Murali secured the silver medal with a best effort of 8.07 metres. Gulveer Singh also added another silver to his tally after finishing runner-up in the men’s 1,500 metres. He had earlier won silver in the men’s 10,000 metres.In shooting, Esha Singh won silver in the women’s 25-metre pistol individual event. The 21-year-old Indian shooter finished second with a score of 38 points.India has moved up to 11th place in the 2026 Asian Games standings, bringing its total medal tally to 47. The current tally includes 5 gold, 21 silver, and 21 bronze medals.President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Neeru Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer on winning the Silver Medal in the Women’s Trap Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the President said that their precision and steady focus have brought this success. President Murmu has wished them to continue to keep their sights set on many more memorable achievements.

. At the Asian Games 2026, the Indian Women’s Compound Archery team clinched gold after beating China 238-234 in the finals today at Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park, Japan. The Indian team, comprising Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep, entered the finals after beating South Korea 234-233 in the semifinals.India won gold in the Women’s compound team event at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou. India is now in ninth position with a total of 53 medals, including seven gold, 21 silver and 25 bronze medals.

. In the Asian Games 2026, India today delivered a strong medal haul, adding eight medals, including two Gold, one Silver and five Bronze medals in relay, shooting, athletics and Boxing. India won the women’s 4 x 400 metre relay, clocking 3 minutes 29.69 seconds at Nagoya in Japan. India also bagged a Bronze in the men’s 4x400m relay and another Bronze in the mixed 4x100m relay.Earlier, Neeru Dhanda made history by becoming the first Indian shooter to win a gold medal in the women’s trap individual event in Japan. This was after she carried India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event with Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer.Gulveer Singh bagged bronze in the men’s 5000 metre final at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is Gulveer’s third medal of the Games after he clinched silver in both the men’s 10,000 metre and 1500m earlier in the competition. Pooja Singh also bagged Bronze in women’s high jump today.In Boxing, Narender Berwal won bronze in men’s boxing plus 90kg category after losing to reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan by a unanimous 0-5 decision in the semi-final today.India has moved up to 10th place in the 2026 Asian Games standings, bringing its total medal tally to 53. The current tally includes 6 gold, 21 silver, and 26 bronze medals.

. India’s Women’s Squash team reached the Asian Games semifinals with a 2-0 win over Singapore today, assuring a medal for the country. Tanvi Khanna beat Au Yeong Wai Iynn 11-6, 4-11, 15-13, 11-1 before Anahat Singh defeated Au Yeong Wai Yhann 11-7, 11-3, 11-4. Veteran Joshna Chinappa did not need to play. India will face its Semifinal opponent at Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena tomorrow. India had topped Pool C after wins over China, Japan and Iran.In Men’s Greco-Roman Wrestling, Sunil Kumar advanced to the Semifinals of 87 kg category today after defeating Tajikistan’s Muhammad Sultonzoda 9-0 by technical superiority in the first period. The 2023 Hangzhou bronze medalist dominated the bout and sealed victory with consecutive gut-wrench moves after Sultonzoda was placed in the par terre position. Sunil is likely to face Japan’s Taizo Yoshida in the Semifinals. However, in the Women’s 68 kg round of 16, Nisha Dahiya lost to North Korea’s Pak Sol Gum.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. Indian High Commissioner Sh. Dinesh Trivedi today held a courtesy meeting with Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr. Humayun Kabir in Dhaka. The High Commissioner congratulated Mr. Kabir on assuming charge as State Minister. During the meeting, the two sides discussed continued cooperation between India and Bangladesh, with a focus on mutually beneficial outcomes for the people of both countries.State Minister Humayun Kabir reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to working with India in a forward-looking and mutually respectful manner on issues of shared interest. The discussions also covered bilateral matters as well as regional and international developments.

. President Droupadi Murmu today congratulated Taniparthi Chikitha, Prithika Pradeep and Jyothi Surekha Vennam on winning the Gold Medal in the Women’s Compound Archery Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the President said that exceptional precision, composure and teamwork of the archers have made the nation proud. She wished that this memorable achievement would inspire them to reach many more milestones.

. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a one MT consignment of GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives. The consignment, exported yesterday by M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, through its Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)-led brand, will be transported to the Maldives by sea. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the initiative is aimed at expanding international markets for India’s GI-tagged agricultural products and strengthening the participation of FPO-led brands in agri exports.It added that a key feature of the export-linked value chain is improved price realisation for farmers, which enables farmers to realise 82 rupees per kg against prevailing market price of 60 rupees per kg. It provides FPOs an opportunity to participate more closely in export-oriented value chains and connect producers with international markets. The Ministry further noted that the export is expected to pave the way for regular shipments of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives, creating sustained market opportunities for producers and exporters from Karnataka. The initiative is also expected to support greater value realisation for farmers and enable FPOs and farmers to integrate more closely with export-oriented value chains.

. The 10th India-Republic of Korea Joint Committee Meeting (JCM) on Defence Industries and Logistics Cooperation was held in New Delhi yesterday. The Defence Ministry said, both countries reviewed the ongoing bilateral cooperation in defence industries and logistics and discussed avenues to further strengthen and expand defence ties. The discussions provided an opportunity to exchange views on enhancing cooperation between the defence industries of the two countries and promoting greater engagement in defence production and logistics.The meeting was co-chaired by Secretary of Defence Production of India, Dinesh Mahur, Additional and Vice Minister of Defence Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Republic of Korea, Kim Il Dong. Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to India, Seong Ho Lee also attended the meeting along with senior officials from both countries.On the sidelines of the JCM, Mr Dong called on Minister of State for Defence Sanjay Seth. During the interaction, both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral defence cooperation and deepening collaboration in defence industries and logistics.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices witnessed a sharp decline and were trading around 1.3% lower during the afternoon session. The Sensex tumbled 956 points to 72,939, while the Nifty shed 306 points to 22,835 when reports last came in.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index fell 1.4%, while the Smallcap 100 index slid 1.6% a short while ago. On the sectoral front, all sectors were trading in the red, as a broad-based sell-off was seen across the board.

. President Droupadi Murmu has congratulated Neeru Dhanda for winning India’s first individual Gold Medal at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the President said that it is a moment of immense pride to see the Tiranga fly high in Aichi-Nagoya. She said that the victory of Neeru Dhanda in the Women’s Trap individual event has set a new Asian record. The President also expressed confidence that this golden moment inspires many more young Indians to take up shooting and strive for excellence.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

The top LeT terrorist was killed in a joint operation by the Army, Police and CRPF in the Yousmarg area of Budgam district during the intervening night.The slain terrorist has been identified as Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) operative Mohammad Asif, alias Hashim Musa.A Srinagar-based Army spokesman said the operation was launched by the Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and CRPF on the basis of specific intelligence inputs. He said that troops observed suspicious activity and, when challenged, terrorists opened fire, leading to an exchange of gunfire in which one terrorist was killed. The operation is in progress.

. In the Asian Games 2026, India today won the women’s 4 x 400 metre relay Gold clocking 3 minutes 29.69 seconds at Nagoya in Japan. India also bagged Bronze in Men’s 4x400m relay. Earlier, Neeru Dhanda made history by becoming the first Indian shooter to win a gold medal in the women’s trap individual event in Japan. This was after she carried India to a silver medal in the women’s trap team event with Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer.Gulveer Singh bagged bronze in the men’s 5000 metre final at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is Gulveer’s third medal of the Games after he clinched silver in both the men’s 10,000 metres and 1,500 metres earlier in the competition. Pooja Singh also bagged Bronze in the women’s high jump today.In Boxing, Narender Berwal won bronze in the men’s boxing plus 90kg category after losing to reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan by a unanimous 0-5 decision in the semi-final today.India has moved up to 10th place in the 2026 Asian Games standings, bringing its total medal tally to 52. The current tally includes 6 gold, 21 silver, and 25 bronze medals.

. Home Minister Amit Shah today congratulated the Indian Women’s Archery Team for winning a gold medal at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that with their stellar performance, the world witnessed India’s chiselled focus on its goal, firmly resolved to remain victorious under immense pressure. Rejoicing the team’s victory, he also wished for more winning sprees ahead in the ongoing games.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya congratulated Sahil Rajesh Jadhav and Chikitha Taniparthi on winning the Gold Medal in the Compound Mixed Team event at Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, he underscored the victory, a monumental one that also secures an LA28 Olympics quota for India.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that India and the United States are witnessing strong momentum in their economic ties.Addressing a Business Roundtable convened by the National Association of Manufacturers in the United States, the Commerce Minister highlighted India’s expanding industrial base and skilled workforce.Mr Goyal also invited American manufacturers to explore opportunities to deepen their presence in India, partner with Indian small and medium enterprises, and co-invest in advanced manufacturing. In a social media post, Mr Goyal said, such cooperation would help build resilient supply chains and create value for both the Indian and US economies.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has described 2026 as a historic year for the Indian Navy, with plans for the induction or commissioning of 18 warships during the year.Addressing the second edition of the Indian Navy’s biannual Commander’s Conference 2026 in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Singh said that the developments reflected the growing maturity of India’s domestic naval shipbuilding ecosystem. Underlining the Navy’s efforts towards achieving self-reliance in the defence sector, the Defence Minister emphasised that the Indian Navy’s warship production ecosystem is now meeting global benchmarks.He said the warships commissioned recently contain over 75 percent indigenous content. The Minister called for a significant upgrade of India’s maritime surveillance architecture, recognising the importance of existing systems. He added that the growing volume and complexity of maritime traffic require enhanced analytical capabilities.Highlighting the government’s commitment to the modernization of the Navy under the leadership of the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Mr Singh stated that the Indian Navy serves as a strategic anchor in the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. He said that the Indian Navy strengthens economic protection, regional stability, and power projection.The Defence Minister has commended the Indian Navy for maintaining a high level of combat readiness and fulfilling its commitments across the region despite evolving challenges. He emphasised that the role of the Indian Navy is crucial in ensuring the strategic depth and regional power projection. The Defence Minister urged the Indian Navy to maintain its unrelenting momentum while transforming itself into a future-ready, combat-ready, and globally respected force.

. At the Asian Games 2026, India’s compound mixed archery team of Sahil Jadhav and Chikitha Taniparthi has won a gold medal, beating Korea in a shoot-off in the finals. The Indian duo also secured a 2028 Olympic quota place with this win. They defeated Thailand in the Semi-finals.Earlier, the Indian Women’s Compound Archery team clinched gold after beating China 238-234 in the finals today at Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park, Japan. The Indian team, comprising Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep, entered the finals after beating South Korea 234-233 in the semifinals. India won gold in the Women’s compound team event at the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou. India now has a total of 54 medals, including eight gold, 21 silver and 25 bronze medals.

. The Election Commission has organised special enrolment camps at colleges and universities in Delhi with the objective of maximising the enrolment of young electors. A large number of students visited the camps yesterday to seek information on the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, and to obtain or submit electoral forms.The camps will continue today as well. The EC said that Block Level Officers, or BLOs, present at these Camps are guiding the students to fill their Forms, collect the filled-in forms and also resolve queries related to SIR. Another round of camps will be organised on 7th and 8th of next month. The poll body requested all young electors to avail this opportunity for enrolment of their names in electoral rolls and participate in the democratic process.Special Camps will also be held at all polling station locations on 4th and 11th of next month for the enrolment of all categories of electors. The Commission said that new applicants attaining the age of 18 years on or before 1st October this year should apply in Form-6 for inclusion of their names in the Electoral Roll. EC noted that as of now, more than four lakh hearings have been conducted in Delhi. The Election Commission also said that electors who have received notices for unmapped or logical discrepancies will be assisted by BLOs, who will visit their homes to collect documents.EC has revised the schedule for the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Delhi. The period for filing claims and objections will continue till 30th of next month, while the final electoral roll will be published on 4th December this year.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

The Supreme Court will tomorrow hear a plea challenging the Centre’s decision to impose a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on specified UPI person-to-merchant transactions of over 2,000 rupees.Ending nearly six years of fully free UPI payments, the government has introduced a 0.4 per cent fee on transfers of over 2,000 Rs made to merchants through the UPI platform from October 15, while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transactions and small payments from any charge. The MDR will be capped at 300 Rs for payments of 75,000 Rs and above.Essential and thin-margin sectors — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs — will pay a flat MDR of 5 Rs per transaction above 2,000 Rs.Payments into mutual funds, securities and through stockbrokers and dealers will attract 0.02 per cent MDR, also capped at 300 Rs. Bench of Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the plea.The Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by advocate Anjan Datta has challenged the Centre’s decision. The plea alleged that the levy has been introduced without adequate statutory safeguards, transparency or public consultation.

. Home Minister Amit Shah is visiting Punjab today to flag in ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatras’ in Jalandhar. The Home Minister will also be at a gathering on the occasion.The Yatras, which were launched by BJP President Nitin Nabin on the 18th of this month from Pathankot, have covered a distance of 4,000 kilometres in all 117 Assembly Constituencies in 13 days. The objective of Yatras was to transform the fight against drugs in Punjab into a people’s movement.These yatras focused on three major challenges Punjab is currently facing, including rising drug abuse, deteriorating law and order and corruption at all levels of governance.

North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) Secretary-General Mark Rutte today accused Russia of carrying out a campaign of hostile actions against NATO allies and said that Moscow was failing to stop the 32-member military alliance’s support for Ukraine. While addressing a joint press conference with Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius, Rutte reiterated NATO’s support for Ukraine and said that Russia is failing on the battlefield in Ukraine and in undermining the military alliance’s support for Kyiv.

. In Men’s Cricket, the second ODI of the three-match series between India and West Indies will be played at Barsapara Cricket Stadium in Guwahati today. The match will begin at 2:00 PM.After a convincing eight-wicket victory in the opening match in Thiruvananthapuram, India aims to extend their lead in the series and establish an insurmountable advantage. With Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill each scoring a century in the first ODI, the hosts are confident going into the second game and looking to continue their strong batting performance.The West Indies, on the other hand, are eager to bounce back after their heavy defeat in the opening match. The visitors will need to improve both their batting and pitching and find a way to contain India’s experienced batsmen. With the series still open, the West Indies are hoping for a significantly improved performance in Guwahati to level the series score.
